method: Editorial filming-location tours for international drama and film fans. Each tour follows scenes from one title within a local outing of one day or less. A title can have multiple tours. Scene evidence and visitor advice are separated; durations are estimates, not live journey times.

routes.title: Lovely Runner
routes.hook: From Sol’s front gate to a riverside confession.
routes.imageCaption: Sun-jae’s confession near Hwahongmun
routes.credit: tvN · reproduced in Hey Roseanne’s location guide
routes.audience: A Filipina traveler based in California documented visiting these locations. TIME also selected the series as its best K-drama of 2024.
routes.audienceKo: 해외 팬의 실제 방문 기록과 해외 매체의 작품 평가를 함께 확인했다. 로맨스 팬을 대상으로 가장 먼저 시험할 후보.
routes.visitNote: Photograph homes from the public street. Café opening hours need a fresh check.

stops.name: Mongted café
stops.scene: The café exterior plays Im Sol’s house. The facing blue gate helps you recognize the neighborhood where their school-day story unfolds.
stops.sceneTitle: Sol’s home, just across from Sun-jae
stops.visit: Look for the entrance from the street, then stop for coffee if the café is open.

stops.name: Haenggung-dong lanes
stops.scene: Sol pushes Sun-jae against a wall to keep him from getting splashed. Their flustered moment was filmed in the lanes around her house.
stops.visit: Begin near Mongted and follow the neighboring lanes; the map opens the wider neighborhood.

stops.name: Hwahongmun stream bridge
stops.scene: On the small pedestrian bridge over Suwoncheon, Sun-jae tells Sol he likes her. Hwahongmun forms the backdrop.
stops.visit: Look for the small stream bridge in front of the gate, rather than the gate itself.

stops.name: Yongyeon Pond
stops.scene: Sun-jae teaches Sol to ride a bicycle along the paths beside Yongyeon Pond.
stops.visit: Follow the pond path below Banghwasuryujeong Pavilion.

routes.seoTitle: Lovely Runner: Sol and Sun-jae’s Suwon Filming Walk
routes.seoDescription: From Sol’s front gate to a riverside confession. Explore Lovely Runner filming locations in Haenggung-dong, Suwon with scene notes and maps.

routes.title: Hometown Cha-Cha-Cha
routes.hook: Market mornings, the hilltop boat and a sea breeze.
routes.imageCaption: Hye-jin and Du-sik’s wedding photos at the hilltop boat
routes.placeCaption: The boat at Sabang Memorial Park
routes.credit: Studio Dragon · still via KTO; location photo via KTO
routes.audience: An English-language Korea travel post specifically considers adding Pohang to a trip because of this drama. Another asks how to reach the locations without renting a car.
routes.audienceKo: 해외 여행 커뮤니티에서 이 작품 때문에 포항을 일정에 넣으려는 질문을 확인했다. 차량 이동 안내가 상품의 중요한 가치가 된다.
routes.visitNote: Book transport between stops. The boat and hilltop viewpoint involve uphill walking. Set dressing can change.

stops.name: Cheongha Market
stops.scene: Cheongha Market stands in for Gongjin’s market, including the settings for Bora Supermarket, Oyun Café and the hardware store.
stops.visit: Walk the market lanes and look for the central squid statue. These remain working premises.

stops.name: Yoon Dental Clinic exterior
stops.scene: The fishermen’s welfare center was dressed as Yoon Dental Clinic, where Hye-jin begins her new life in Gongjin.
stops.visit: View the exterior from the public street. Interior access is not part of this route.

stops.name: Sabang Memorial Park
stops.scene: The boat on Mugeunbong is Chief Hong’s hilltop retreat. It also appears in the couple’s wedding-photo scene.
stops.visit: Walk uphill from Sabang Memorial Park for the boat and coastal backdrop.

sources.label: Reddit · adding Pohang for the drama
Reddit · visiting without a rental car

routes.seoTitle: Hometown Cha-Cha-Cha: A Day in Gongjin, Pohang
routes.seoDescription: Market mornings, the hilltop boat and a sea breeze. Explore Hometown Cha-Cha-Cha filming locations in Cheongha and Cheongjin, Pohang with scene notes and maps.

routes.title: Goblin
routes.course: Where the sea meets the forest
routes.hook: Follow the forest confession and the seaside flower encounter.
routes.imageCaption: Jumunjin Breakwater, the iconic seaside filming spot
routes.audience: Viki’s international audience page shows a 9.7 rating at the time of research. This indicates an established fan audience, not measured demand for this itinerary.
routes.audienceKo: Viki의 해외 팬 평점으로 작품 선호를 확인했다. 꽃을 들고 장면을 재현하는 경험을 시험할 후보이며 코스 구매 수요는 아직 확인하지 않았다.
routes.visitNote: The forest and coast are separate driving stops. Avoid the breakwater when waves or access restrictions make it unsafe.

stops.name: Woljeongsa fir forest
stops.scene: The fir-tree path is the setting for Kim Shin and Eun-tak’s romantic forest scene, where they confirm their feelings.
stops.sceneTitle: A promise in the snowy forest
stops.visit: Follow the marked forest path. Snow depends on the season; the scene’s winter setting is not year-round.

stops.name: Jumunjin Breakwater
stops.scene: The breakwater is the setting for Kim Shin and Eun-tak’s seaside encounter, remembered for the buckwheat flowers.
stops.visit: Find the filming breakwater near Yeongjin Beach. Stay ashore if waves or access restrictions make the pier unsafe.

routes.seoTitle: Goblin: Gangwon Forest and Sea Filming Tour
routes.seoDescription: Follow the forest confession and the seaside flower encounter. Explore Goblin filming locations in Pyeongchang and Gangneung with scene notes and maps.

routes.title: Our Beloved Summer
routes.course: The long way back to you
routes.hook: Ung’s neighborhood, fortress walks and Yeon-su’s green gate.
routes.imageCaption: Jidong’s residential lanes near Yeon-su’s house
routes.audience: A CIEE study-abroad participant documented a dedicated trip to the show’s locations and meeting other fans there.
routes.audienceKo: 미국에서 온 교환학생의 촬영지 방문 기록을 확인했다. 조용한 동네 산책과 사진을 좋아하는 팬에게 맞는 후보.
routes.visitNote: Both home stops are exterior-only concepts. Keep entrances clear and respect residents.

stops.name: Choi Ung’s house exterior
stops.scene: The white-walled building appears as Choi Ung’s home, one of the recurring settings in his story with Yeon-su.
stops.visit: Enjoy the exterior from the street; do not assume the former café is operating.

stops.name: Hwaseong Fortress walk
stops.scene: Hwaseong’s surroundings connect the couple’s home locations and date settings. This stop explores the filming area rather than a single confirmed camera position.
stops.visit: Take the fortress-side path through Hwahongmun toward Jidong.

stops.name: Yeon-su’s house lane
stops.scene: The green gate beside Jidong Supermarket appears as Yeon-su’s home. The nearby rainbow mural recurs in neighborhood scenes.
stops.visit: Keep the lane and residents’ doorways clear when taking a photo.

routes.seoTitle: Our Beloved Summer: Suwon Reunion Filming Walk
routes.seoDescription: Ung’s neighborhood, fortress walks and Yeon-su’s green gate. Explore Our Beloved Summer filming locations in Hwaseong Fortress, Suwon with scene notes and maps.

routes.title: Itaewon Class
routes.hook: Find DanBam, then take in Saeroyi’s city skyline.
routes.imageCaption: The DanBam filming exterior as shown in KTO’s guide
routes.audience: Netflix included Itaewon Class among the K-dramas competing strongly in Southeast Asian Top 10 lists in 2020.
routes.audienceKo: 동남아 시청 반응이 확인되는 작품이다. 짧은 야간 산책에 식사를 붙이기 쉬워 첫 한국 여행객에게 제안할 만하다.
routes.visitNote: The photographed business name and façade may have changed. The course does not assume the filming restaurant still operates.

stops.name: DanBam filming exterior
stops.scene: Saeroyi and Soo-ah meet again outside the pub at the end of episode 2. The exterior becomes a familiar backdrop to his new start.
stops.visit: Match the building at 57 Noksapyeong-daero 40-gil; the current business may differ.

stops.name: Noksapyeong footbridge
stops.scene: On the pedestrian overpass, Saeroyi admits that he needs Yi-seo. The city lights and Namsan Tower frame the scene.
stops.visit: Cross the public footbridge and keep its walking lane clear.

routes.seoTitle: Itaewon Class: DanBam and New Beginnings in Seoul
routes.seoDescription: Find DanBam, then take in Saeroyi’s city skyline. Explore Itaewon Class filming locations in Itaewon, Seoul with scene notes and maps.

routes.title: Vincenzo
routes.hook: Walk into the plaza, then follow the city after dark.
routes.imageCaption: Vincenzo at Geumga Plaza
routes.placeCaption: Cheonggye building in the Sewoon complex
routes.credit: Studio Dragon · still via KTO; location photo via KTO
routes.audience: What’s on Netflix’s 2021 review reports sustained Top 10 presence in Vietnam, Japan, Thailand and Malaysia. This is historical viewing evidence, not a current tourism demand count.
routes.audienceKo: 2021년 해외 넷플릭스 순위 분석에서 아시아 시청 반응을 확인했다. 송중기 팬을 대상으로 도심 코스 수요를 시험할 후보.
routes.visitNote: Use public walkways in the working mall. Bank of Korea is an exterior stop; no interior scene access is promised.

stops.name: Geumga Plaza exterior
stops.scene: The Cheonggye building in the Sewoon complex doubles as Geumga Plaza, the central setting shared by Vincenzo and its tenants.
stops.visit: Explore public walkways around the working shopping complex.

stops.name: Bank of Korea exterior
stops.scene: The Bank of Korea’s historic building provides the setting for Woosang, the law firm allied with Babel.
stops.visit: This is an exterior stop. A museum visit does not provide access to the drama’s office sets.

stops.name: Seoullo 7017
stops.scene: The illuminated elevated walkway is where Vincenzo walks alone through the city at night.
stops.visit: Follow the pedestrian path above the streets near Seoul Station.

sources.label: What’s on Netflix · 2021 overseas viewing analysis

routes.seoTitle: Vincenzo: Geumga Plaza and Central Seoul Filming Tour
routes.seoDescription: Walk into the plaza, then follow the city after dark. Explore Vincenzo filming locations in Central Seoul with scene notes and maps.

routes.title: Crash Landing on You
routes.hook: A reunion bench, a lakeside walk and a second love story.
routes.imageCaption: Tangeumho Rainbow Road after dark
routes.audience: Netflix reported the drama reaching Top 10 lists in the Philippines, Singapore, Taiwan and Thailand.
routes.audienceKo: 해외 인지도는 높다. 한국 안에서 방문 가능한 재회 장면과 서브 커플의 장면으로 코스를 구성했다.
routes.visitNote: Plan travel to Chungju separately. Lighting and lakeside access can change with weather and maintenance.

stops.name: Jungangtap Park
stops.scene: Se-ri and Jeong-hyeok reunite with his men at Jungangtap Park during the South Korea part of the story.
stops.visit: Look for the filming bench along the riverside park.

stops.name: Tangeumho Rainbow Road
stops.scene: The lakeside bridge is the setting where the second couple share their feelings.
stops.visit: Walk the bridge around dusk; decorative lighting may vary.

routes.seoTitle: Crash Landing on You: Chungju Reunion Filming Tour
routes.seoDescription: A reunion bench, a lakeside walk and a second love story. Explore Crash Landing on You filming locations in Chungju with scene notes and maps.

routes.title: Extraordinary Attorney Woo
routes.hook: A temple path, a window through the rocks and time by the sea.
routes.imageCaption: Changkkom’s window-shaped rock
routes.audience: Netflix ranked the series first on its weekly non-English TV list for the week of August 15, 2022.
routes.audienceKo: 글로벌 시청 성과가 있는 작품이다. 제주 출장 에피소드의 장소를 묶되 직접적인 해외 방문 수요는 추가 검증할 후보.
routes.visitNote: Travel between the temple and north-coast filming spot by car or booked taxi. Hamdeok Beach can be an optional food break afterward.

stops.name: Gwaneumsa Temple
stops.scene: Gwaneumsa plays the fictional Hwangjisa Temple during the legal team’s Jeju business trip.
stops.visit: Walk the approach and temple grounds quietly; it is an active place of worship.

stops.name: Changkkom
stops.scene: At the window-shaped coastal rock, Jung Myeong-seok recalls memories of his wife.
stops.visit: Look through the opening toward the sea. Stay on accessible paths around the rocks.

routes.seoTitle: Extraordinary Attorney Woo: Jeju Temple and Coast Tour
routes.seoDescription: A temple path, a window through the rocks and time by the sea. Explore Extraordinary Attorney Woo filming locations in Jeju City with scene notes and maps.

routes.title: Squid Game
routes.hook: The everyday streets before the games begin.
routes.imageCaption: Paldo Dried Seafood, the shop used as Sang-woo’s mother’s store
routes.audience: Netflix reported Season 2 reaching the Top 10 in 93 countries in the week beginning December 30, 2024. This itinerary follows Season 1’s real neighborhood locations.
routes.audienceKo: 해외 인지도가 높은 입구 상품 후보다. 시장과 편의점 장면을 중심으로 하며 게임장 세트 방문을 약속하지 않는다.
routes.visitNote: These are working shops. Confirm the current business and get permission before photographing staff or customers.

stops.name: Baegun Market / Paldo Dried Seafood
stops.scene: Paldo Dried Seafood doubles as Sang-woo’s mother’s shop, which Gi-hun visits in the neighborhood outside the games.
stops.visit: Find the storefront inside Baegun Market; ask before photographing people.

stops.name: CU Ssangmun Uicheon filming site
stops.scene: After the first game, Gi-hun and Il-nam meet again outside this convenience store and talk over noodles and soju.
stops.visit: View the storefront from the public pavement. The business and outdoor seating may have changed.

routes.seoTitle: Squid Game: Gi-hun’s Ssangmun Neighbourhood Walk
routes.seoDescription: The everyday streets before the games begin. Explore Squid Game filming locations in Ssangmun-dong, Seoul with scene notes and maps.

routes.title: It’s Okay to Not Be Okay
routes.course: A quiet day by the sea
routes.hook: The hospital garden and the beach from their escape.
routes.imageCaption: Ayajin Beach
routes.audience: Netflix said the show spent over 100 days in the Top 10 in Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore and Thailand in 2020.
routes.audienceKo: 동남아 장기 시청 반응이 확인된다. 바다와 카페를 좋아하는 팬에게 제안할 수 있지만 현재 현장 이용 조건은 재확인이 필요하다.
routes.visitNote: Check Secret Blue’s current operation and garden access before travel. Interior access and surviving set props are not confirmed.

stops.name: Secret Blue café site
stops.scene: The café grounds play the hospital exterior and garden, a recurring setting around Gang-tae’s work.
stops.sceneTitle: The garden at OK Psychiatric Hospital
stops.visit: Check the current café operation and garden access before visiting.

stops.name: Ayajin Beach
stops.scene: At the end of episode 8, Gang-tae tells Mun-yeong he wants to take a trip with her, with Ayajin’s sea in view.
stops.sceneTitle: A smile and a promise to get away
stops.visit: End with a walk on the public beachfront.

routes.seoTitle: It’s Okay to Not Be Okay: Goseong Seaside Filming Tour
routes.seoDescription: The hospital garden and the beach from their escape. Explore It’s Okay to Not Be Okay filming locations in Ayajin, Goseong with scene notes and maps.

routes.title: Queen of Tears
routes.hook: A department store empire and the garden behind the family’s grand home.
routes.imageCaption: The Hyundai Seoul interior, a filming location for Queens department store.
routes.audience: Selected for international fans of Korean screen stories; this is an editorial selection, not a popularity ranking.
routes.visitNote: These are public venues used for selected shots; neither contains the complete fictional mansion or store.

stops.name: The Hyundai Seoul
stops.scene: The atrium and retail spaces stand in for Queens Department Store, where Hae-in leads the family business.
stops.visit: Explore the public shopping floors. The fictional rooftop is a separate filming location.

stops.name: Korean Stone Art Museum
stops.scene: The museum’s stone garden and exterior were used for the Queens family mansion.
stops.visit: Check museum admission before travelling uphill. Follow visitor paths in the garden.

routes.seoTitle: Queen of Tears: Queens Department Store and Garden Tour
routes.seoDescription: A department store empire and the garden behind the family’s grand home. Explore Queen of Tears filming locations in Seoul with scene notes and maps.

routes.title: Business Proposal
routes.course: When the fake date becomes real
routes.hook: Flowers in the rain, then a carefree theme-park date.
routes.imageCaption: Lotte World Adventure, the theme park used for Tae-moo and Ha-ri’s date.
routes.audience: Selected for international fans of Korean screen stories; this is an editorial selection, not a popularity ranking.
routes.visitNote: Allow a full day if you want rides. Flowers and theme-park admission are separate purchases.

stops.name: Yangjae Flower Market
stops.scene: Tae-mu buys Ha-ri flowers while they shelter from the rain at the flower market.
stops.visit: Start in the morning and check which flower-market halls are open.

stops.name: Lotte World Adventure
stops.scene: Ha-ri and Tae-mu’s amusement-park date brings them to the bumper cars and merry-go-round.
stops.visit: Admission is required. Ride queues can add several hours.

routes.seoTitle: Business Proposal: Seoul Flower and Theme Park Date
routes.seoDescription: Flowers in the rain, then a carefree theme-park date. Explore Business Proposal filming locations in Yangjae and Jamsil, Seoul with scene notes and maps.

routes.title: King the Land
routes.hook: An island bicycle date and a photo beneath a heart-shaped tree.
routes.imageCaption: Sono Calm Jeju, the King Hotel promotional-shoot location.
routes.credit: Photo via VISITKOREA / Korea Tourism Organization
routes.audience: Selected for international fans of Korean screen stories; this is an editorial selection, not a popularity ranking.
routes.visitNote: Gapado ferries depend on weather. Leave substantial driving time between western and eastern Jeju.

stops.name: Gapado Island
stops.sceneTitle: A bicycle date on the island
stops.scene: Gu Won and Sa-rang’s bicycle date unfolds on Gapado’s quiet island roads.
stops.visit: Book a morning ferry and check return sailings before renting bicycles.

stops.name: Sono Calm Jeju
stops.scene: The pair film King Hotel’s promotional video here and pose at the heart-shaped tree.
stops.visit: Ask the resort about garden access for day visitors before making the cross-island drive.

routes.seoTitle: King the Land: Gapado and Southern Jeju Date Tour
routes.seoDescription: An island bicycle date and a photo beneath a heart-shaped tree. Explore King the Land filming locations in Southern Jeju with scene notes and maps.

routes.title: Twenty-Five Twenty-One
routes.hook: A white gate, a tunnel and the little shop where friends gathered.
routes.imageCaption: Hanbyeok Tunnel, where Hee-do and Yi-jin share their feelings.
routes.credit: Photo via VISITKOREA / Korea Tourism Organization
routes.audience: Selected for international fans of Korean screen stories; this is an editorial selection, not a popularity ranking.
routes.visitNote: The story is set in Seoul, but these scenes were filmed in Jeonju.

stops.name: Hee-do’s house exterior
stops.sceneTitle: The gate where they first meet
stops.scene: The white-gated house near the hanok village is where Hee-do and Yi-jin first meet.
stops.visit: View the gate from the public lane; do not enter the former guesthouse.

stops.name: Hanbyeok Tunnel
stops.sceneTitle: Love and goodbye in the same tunnel
stops.scene: The tunnel becomes a recurring place for Hee-do and Yi-jin to share feelings, and later to part.
stops.visit: Stay aware of passing traffic and keep the tunnel entrance clear.

stops.name: Ahyeon Supermarket set
stops.sceneTitle: A place to sit with friends
stops.scene: The group’s neighborhood store and bench were recreated here after filming ended.
stops.visit: Treat this as a reconstructed fan stop and check current access.

routes.seoTitle: Twenty-Five Twenty-One: Jeonju First Love Filming Walk
routes.seoDescription: A white gate, a tunnel and the little shop where friends gathered. Explore Twenty-Five Twenty-One filming locations in Jeonju with scene notes and maps.

routes.title: True Beauty
routes.course: A secret shared between the pages
routes.hook: Follow Ju-kyung and Su-ho from the comic shop to the walk home.
routes.imageCaption: Prince Comic Rental Shop exterior on Yunboseon-gil.
routes.credit: Photo via VISITKOREA / Korea Tourism Organization
routes.audience: Selected for international fans of Korean screen stories; this is an editorial selection, not a popularity ranking.
routes.visitNote: Bukchon is a residential neighborhood. Follow posted visitor hours and stay on public streets.

stops.name: Prince Comic Rental Shop exterior
stops.scene: This hanok storefront becomes the comic rental shop where Ju-kyung and Su-ho repeatedly meet.
stops.visit: The building is a real shop. Ask before taking photographs inside.

stops.name: Yunboseon-gil stone-wall lane
stops.scene: The stone-wall road beside the comic shop appears along Seo-jun’s motorcycle route.
stops.visit: Keep to the side of the narrow public lane.

stops.name: Sosho Gallery exterior
stops.scene: The gallery exterior stands in for Ju-kyung’s house during their walks home.
stops.visit: Plan for an exterior view only. Respect residential quiet hours.

routes.seoTitle: True Beauty: Anguk Comic Shop and Secret Filming Walk
routes.seoDescription: Follow Ju-kyung and Su-ho from the comic shop to the walk home. Explore True Beauty filming locations in Anguk, Seoul with scene notes and maps.

routes.title: Hotel del Luna
routes.hook: Trace the hotel’s past, then visit a library of unfinished wishes.
routes.imageCaption: Seoul Book Bogo, the grandmother ghost’s bookshop
routes.audience: Selected for international fans of Korean screen stories; this is an editorial selection, not a popularity ranking.
routes.visitNote: The two places represent different memories in the drama. Allow subway travel between Jongno and Jamsil.

stops.name: Hotel Seine café
stops.scene: Hotel Seine appears in the historical photographs that record the changing life of Man-wol’s hotel.
stops.visit: It is a café, not the full hotel set. Order if you use its seating.

stops.name: Seoul Book Bogo
stops.sceneTitle: The grandmother who wanted to read
stops.scene: The arched secondhand-bookshop aisles appear in the story of the grandmother ghost who regrets missing an education.
stops.visit: Check the bookstore’s current visitor notice before travelling across town.

routes.seoTitle: Hotel del Luna: Seoul’s Hotel and Bookshop Memories Tour
routes.seoDescription: Trace the hotel’s past, then visit a library of unfinished wishes. Explore Hotel del Luna filming locations in Seoul with scene notes and maps.

routes.title: My Love from the Star

stops.name: Hakrim Dabang

stops.name: N Seoul Tower

routes.seoTitle: My Love from the Star: Seoul Café and Tower Date Tour
routes.seoDescription: A trusted friend over coffee, then a promise above the city. Explore My Love from the Star filming locations in Daehangno and Namsan, Seoul with scene notes and maps.

routes.audience: Selected for international fans of Korean screen stories; this is an editorial selection, not a popularity ranking.

stops.name: Sunshine Studio streets

stops.scene: These purpose-built streets recreate early twentieth-century Hanseong for the drama’s encounters and political tensions.

routes.seoDescription: Walk the streets of a changing country, then pause at the Glory Hotel. Explore Mr. Sunshine filming locations in Sunshine Studio, Nonsan with scene notes and maps.

routes.title: Reply 1988
routes.hook: Two café dates from the quieter side of growing up.
routes.imageCaption: Brown Hands Dogok, where Jung-bong and Mi-ok’s first kiss was filmed

routes.seoTitle: My Demon: Seoul Forest & Ttukseom Date Filming Tour
routes.seoDescription: Follow Gu-won and Do-hee’s quieter date scenes through Seoul Forest’s Mirror Pond and nearby Ttukseom Hangang Park on an easy half-day Seoul route.

stops.name: Seoul Forest Mirror Pond
stops.scene: Gu-won and Do-hee spend their date at the Mirror Pond as they try enjoying everyday things together.
stops.visit: Find the Mirror Pond inside Seoul Forest’s Cultural Art Park; follow posted paths around the water.

stops.name: Ttukseom Hangang Park
stops.sceneTitle: The riverside part of their date
stops.scene: The couple’s outdoor date also uses Ttukseom Hangang Park beside the Han River.
stops.visit: Enter near Jayang Station and follow the river paths. The exact camera position is not marked.

routes.title: Encounter
routes.course: From an art date to a goodbye
routes.hook: Walk the stream where they fall closer, then find the address of their last café date.
routes.visitNote: Stamp Coffee is listed as closed. This route includes its former address for an exterior stop only, not a café visit. Art displays and the storefront may differ from the drama.
routes.imageCaption: Hongjecheon’s bridge pillars and streamside art-date setting
routes.audience: Selected for international fans of Korean screen stories; this is an editorial selection, not a popularity ranking.
routes.seoTitle: Encounter: Hongjecheon Art Date & Yeonnam Filming Walk
routes.seoDescription: Relive Encounter’s Hongjecheon art date and visit the former Stamp Coffee address in Yeonnam-dong on a short Seoul route; the café itself has closed.

stops.name: Hongjecheon near Hongnamgyo Bridge
stops.scene: Jin-hyuk brings Soo-hyun to the streamside art display, where they pause over a work by Kim Whanki.
stops.visit: Walk the path under and near Hongnamgyo Bridge and look at the paintings on the supporting pillars.

stops.name: Former Stamp Coffee exterior
stops.scene: Before their breakup, Soo-hyun and Jin-hyuk share their last café date at Stamp Coffee.
stops.visit: The café is listed as closed. Make only a brief public-street stop at 161-7 Seongmisan-ro; do not expect the original interior.

routes.title: Fight for My Way
routes.hook: Find the neighborhood above the city where friends share beer, worries and dreams.
routes.transport: Walk; taxi or local bus uphill
routes.visitNote: The original Namil Bar is a private rooftop and can only be viewed from the public street. The cultural platform has a separate replica. The village has steep stairs and occupied homes.
routes.imageCaption: Hocheon Village’s 180 Stairs, identified by Visit Busan as an on-screen location
routes.audience: Selected for international fans of Korean screen stories; this is an editorial selection, not a popularity ranking.
routes.seoTitle: Fight for My Way: Busan’s Hocheon Rooftop & Stairs Walk
routes.seoDescription: Explore Fight for My Way’s Hocheon Village in Busan, linking the on-screen 180 Stairs with an outside view of the original Namil Bar rooftop in one short walk.

stops.name: Hocheon Village 180 Stairs
stops.scene: These long hillside steps appear in Fight for My Way, placing the story among Hocheon’s closely packed homes.
stops.visit: Start from the upper end near Hocheon Cultural Platform. Descend only as far as comfortable; the steps are steep.

stops.name: Original Namil Bar rooftop, exterior view
stops.sceneTitle: Friends share their worries above the city
stops.scene: The friends gather at Namil Bar for beer, food and conversations about their troubles against the night skyline.
stops.visit: From the cultural platform, follow the tiger-mural lane to the original rooftop house. View from the public street; do not enter the home or climb its stairs.

sources.label: Visit Busan · original rooftop and replica distinction

routes.title: Welcome to Samdal-ri
routes.course: Finding the way home with Sam-dal
routes.hook: From the village gathering place to the coast where her photographs find a future.
routes.transport: Short taxi or car ride + walk
routes.visitNote: A short Seongsan-area outing with an estimated 10–15-minute drive between stops. Ojo is a working harbor; screen props and shopfronts can change. Stay on public paths and check coastal weather.

stops.name: Ojo Port
stops.sceneTitle: Back with the Five Eagle Brothers
stops.scene: The harbor supplied the setting for the Samdal-ri bus stop and Lucky Convenience Store, where the childhood friends gather.
stops.visit: Explore the public harbor edge and look across the inlet toward Seongsan Ilchulbong.

stops.name: Gwangchigi Beach coast
stops.sceneTitle: A new start through her photographs
stops.scene: Sam-dal and Yong-pil travel this coastal stretch to submit her Jeju photographs to the weather agency competition.
stops.visit: Take a short shore walk after the drive; avoid slippery exposed rocks.

routes.seoTitle: Welcome to Samdal-ri: Coming Home in Seongsan, Jeju
routes.seoDescription: Follow Sam-dal home in Seongsan, Jeju, from Ojo Port’s village gathering place to Gwangchigi’s photo-contest drive on a relaxed two-stop afternoon.
routes.imageCaption: Ojo Port, the harbor behind Samdal-ri’s village gathering place.
routes.credit: Photo via VisitJeju / Jeju Tourism Organization
routes.audience: Selected for international fans of Korean screen stories; this is an editorial selection, not a popularity ranking.

routes.title: When Life Gives You Tangerines
routes.course: Waiting for Eun-myeong to come home
routes.hook: Follow Ae-sun’s working day to the harbor where the family welcomes their son.
routes.visitNote: Both stops are in the same harbor district; allow roughly 15–25 minutes for the connecting walk. Use public market and waterfront areas. The ice factory and operational quays are workplaces, not visitor attractions.

stops.name: Hallim Fisheries Market
stops.scene: Ae-sun sells squid here, and Eun-myeong’s ice-factory work belongs to this market setting.
stops.visit: Walk the public market area; ask before photographing vendors.

stops.name: Hallim Port
stops.sceneTitle: Their son returns from the sea
stops.scene: Ae-sun and Gwan-sik welcome Eun-myeong back from deep-sea fishing at this port.
stops.visit: Continue to the public waterfront and watch the fishing boats from a safe distance.

sources.label: VisitJeju · Hallim market and reunion scenes

routes.seoTitle: When Life Gives You Tangerines: Hallim Family Reunion Walk
routes.seoDescription: Walk Hallim’s market and harbor in Jeju, tracing Ae-sun’s squid-selling days and Eun-myeong’s return from sea on a gentle two-stop family-story tour.
routes.imageCaption: Fishing boats at Hallim Port, where the family welcomes Eun-myeong home.
routes.credit: Photo via VisitJeju / Jeju Tourism Organization
routes.audience: Selected for international fans of Korean screen stories; this is an editorial selection, not a popularity ranking.

routes.title: Our Blues
routes.course: After the auction, room for love
routes.hook: Meet the working coast before following Yeong-ok and Jeong-jun to the shallows.
routes.transport: Short taxi or car ride + walk
routes.visitNote: Keep this trip on Jeju’s west coast, with an estimated 15–20-minute drive between stops. Auction access is not guaranteed. Enjoy Geumneung from shore unless swimming is permitted and conditions are safe.

stops.name: Hallim Port
stops.scene: The opening episode’s fish-auction scene was filmed at Hallim Port, introducing the labor behind the island’s daily life.
stops.visit: Stay along the public waterfront; do not enter working auction or loading areas without permission.

stops.name: Geumneung Beach
stops.scene: This shallow coast is the setting where the new haenyeo and the young boat captain develop feelings for each other.
stops.visit: Walk the sand and look toward Biyangdo; allow time to sit by the sea.

routes.seoTitle: Our Blues: A Hallim and Geumneung Afternoon in Jeju
routes.seoDescription: Explore Our Blues on Jeju’s west coast: Hallim’s fish-auction setting and Yeong-ok and Jeong-jun’s Geumneung shore, linked by a short afternoon drive.
routes.imageCaption: Hallim Port, the setting of the opening fish auction.
routes.credit: Photo via VISITKOREA / Korea Tourism Organization
routes.audience: Selected for international fans of Korean screen stories; this is an editorial selection, not a popularity ranking.

routes.title: Descendants of the Sun
routes.course: A day of duty in Uruk
routes.hook: Walk between the medical team’s base and the soldiers’ quarters at Taebaek’s reconstructed set.
routes.visitNote: The original set was dismantled and this visitor set was reconstructed. Both stops are within Tongri Tantan Park, a single attraction. Check park admission and access before traveling; the cover is an archive photograph.

stops.name: Medi Cube compound
stops.scene: The reconstructed medical compound recalls the base where the volunteer doctors work in the drama’s fictional Uruk.
stops.visit: Follow the park signs to the white medical containers; enter only visitor-accessible rooms.

stops.name: Uruk military barracks
stops.scene: The neighboring reconstructed barracks evoke the soldiers’ base alongside the medical team, linking Shi-jin’s duty with Mo-yeon’s work.
stops.visit: Continue on foot within the same set; allow extra time if interiors are open.

sources.label: Taebaek City · reconstructed Descendants of the Sun set

routes.seoTitle: Descendants of the Sun: Taebaek’s Recreated Uruk Base
routes.seoDescription: Recall Shi-jin and Mo-yeon’s Uruk mission in Taebaek with a short walk between the reconstructed Medi Cube and barracks inside Tongri Tantan Park.
routes.imageCaption: The reconstructed Medi Cube and barracks at Taebaek’s Uruk set.
routes.audience: Selected for international fans of Korean screen stories; this is an editorial selection, not a popularity ranking.

routes.title: Winter Sonata
routes.course: Before the years came between them
routes.hook: Follow the island paths back to Jun-sang and Yu-jin’s first kiss.
routes.visitNote: Both stops are on Nami Island. The estimate covers the ferry and island walk, excluding travel to Gapyeong. Check the last return ferry; snow and autumn colors are seasonal. Follow the island’s current filming-location signs.

stops.name: Metasequoia Lane
stops.scene: Nami Island’s tree-lined avenue appears in the drama and frames a return to Jun-sang and Yu-jin’s youthful romance.
stops.visit: Walk beneath the tall trees, keeping the central path clear for other visitors.

stops.name: Winter Sonata first-kiss site
stops.sceneTitle: The snowmen and the first kiss
stops.scene: After skipping their classroom-cleaning punishment, Jun-sang and Yu-jin share their first kiss beside the snowmen on a bench.
stops.visit: Use the island map to find the marked first-kiss site; the visitor display may differ from the original filming props.

sources.label: KBS World · director recalls the first-kiss scene
KBS World · visiting Nami filming sites

routes.seoTitle: Winter Sonata: Nami Island’s First-Love Walk
routes.seoDescription: Return to Jun-sang and Yu-jin’s first love on Nami Island, Chuncheon, with a ferry trip and easy walk from Metasequoia Lane to the first-kiss site.
routes.imageCaption: Autumn on Nami Island’s Metasequoia Lane.

routes.title: Dae Jang Geum
routes.course: The exile that opens a new calling
routes.hook: Return to the Jeju chapter where Jang-geum begins learning medicine from Jang-deok.
routes.visitNote: This short tour stays within one filming location. Follow the Dae Jang Geum scene panels around the traditional houses. The mini theme park is an optional exhibition visit, with costumes, scripts and medical objects. Check village admission before arrival.

stops.name: Dae Jang Geum filming houses, Jeju Folk Village
stops.scene: Jang-geum’s Jeju exile and her medical training under Jang-deok were filmed among these traditional houses. The scene panels reconnect the village with that turning point.
stops.visit: Follow the signed filming trail at an unhurried pace; use the on-site panels to identify the featured houses.

sources.label: VisitJeju · exile and medical-training filming location

routes.seoTitle: Dae Jang Geum: A New Calling at Jeju Folk Village
routes.seoDescription: Follow Jang-geum’s exile and medical training with Jang-deok at Jeju Folk Village in Pyoseon, a gentle one-to-two-hour walk through the filming houses.
routes.imageCaption: Traditional houses and a Dae Jang Geum scene panel at Jeju Folk Village.
routes.credit: Photo via VisitJeju / Jeju Tourism Organization

routes.title: Kingdom
routes.course: The gates between a plague and the capital
routes.hook: Walk the mountain passage that stands between Lee Chang’s journey and the spreading outbreak.
routes.visitNote: A local walking tour, with roughly 8 km out and back from the park entrance to the second gate. Allow for a steady uphill approach and the return walk. Stay on the main trail and check weather and access notices.

stops.name: Juheulgwan, First Gate
stops.scene: Soldiers line this gate as Cho Hak-ju moves to contain the plague. The drama expands the fortress with visual effects.
stops.visit: Approach from the park entrance and pause before the gate to recognize its defensive outline.

stops.name: Jogokgwan, Second Gate
stops.scene: The second gate appears in a horseback departure scene on the dangerous route toward Hanyang.
stops.visit: Continue along the main mountain-pass trail, then return the same way; carry water and wear walking shoes.

routes.seoTitle: Kingdom: Walk the Plague-Defense Gates of Mungyeongsaejae
routes.seoDescription: Trace Kingdom’s plague-defense scenes through Juheulgwan and Jogokgwan in Mungyeongsaejae, an out-and-back mountain-pass walk within a single day.
